resumen: Which part of the photo the camera measures and when to change modes.

bloques.alt: Three photos of the same scene, a backlit person, with the area the camera measures marked. On the left, evaluative metering measures the whole scene: 1, evaluative. In the middle, center-weighted metering gives more weight to the center of the image: 2, center. On the right, spot metering measures just one small point, on the face: 3, spot.
bloques.pie: 1 Evaluative: the whole scene. 2 Center: the center counts more. 3 Spot: one small point.

bloques.texto: Metering decides which part of the photo drives the exposure calculation. Evaluative is fine almost always; change it when the subject and the background have very different light.

The camera measures the light and tries to make the scene come out a middle gray. The [[medicion|metering]] mode tells it which part of the frame to measure and how much each part counts. Each brand names them its own way.

items: Evaluative (or matrix): it measures the whole scene at once and is usually the default. It works for almost everything, but gets fooled by very bright or very dark scenes.
Center-weighted: it gives more weight to the center of the image. It suits a centered subject, like a portrait.

Spot: it measures just one small point, which on many cameras follows the focus point. It is the most precise: use it when the subject and the background have very different light, like the moon in a dark sky or a backlit face. But everything else can come out very bright or very dark.
Partial: like spot, but with a somewhat bigger area. Not every camera has it.

bloques.texto: Put the point on what you want well exposed, lock the exposure with the [[bloqueo-ae-af|AE/AF lock]] and frame as you like.

The meter wants a middle gray: snow comes out gray and something very dark comes out too bright. Fix it with [[compensacion|compensation]]: raise the exposure with snow and lower it with dark things. Metering only decides where the calculation comes from; compensation corrects it.
Tapping the screen measures at that point: see “Tap to focus and expose”.
Put someone in backlight. Take one photo with evaluative and another with spot on their face. Compare.
